doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

chapter: Early New Orleans experiences and sideman roles
title: Danny Barker, Erroll Garner and music without schooling
summary: Garner could not read music; Barker and Blue Lu Barker as examples of New Orleans musicianship unsullied by education.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Reeves and through just various associations, been very fortunate to have had the chance to play with some iconic musicians.
Did — I’m not sure how to phrase this question. But Danny Barker and Erroll Garner, they obviously didn’t go to Berklee. They didn’t?
Oh no, no. As a matter of fact Erroll Garner didn’t — couldn’t read music.
That’s what I’m trying to get at.

And Danny Barker could read chord changes, but he was a very natural musician. But that’s another example of what I was talking about earlier as far as New Orleans musicians affecting — their culture affecting — like for instance Danny Barker moved to New York, played with Charlie Parker, played with Cab Calloway, he played behind Billie Holiday. His wife, Blue Lu Barker, is cited by Billie Holiday as being one of her major early influences as far as how she approached — and you know Blue Lu Barker came out, she came out in New Orleans, you know from the New Orleans streets. It was completely unsullied by music education. It was purely from the human experience, and their particular human experience that happens in humidity, it happens in the social economic tension that’s in New Orleans, you know, not racial per se, but it’s a very complex and ever-changing myriad of energies. Not to sound too metaphysical.
